leftEvidence.title: Peter says God fulfilled what all the prophets announced about the Christ’s suffering

points.label: Actors named
points.left: God, the patriarchs, Jesus, Pilate, the crowd, and the prophets enter Peter’s speech.
points.right: The speaker, the servant, “we,” the LORD, oppressors, and later offspring enter Isaiah’s poem.

points.label: Suffering language
points.left: Peter names betrayal, denial, killing, and prophetic announcement.
points.right: Isaiah names rejection, wounds, oppression, silence, grave, bearing, and vindication.

payload.posture: The sources independently preserve the relationship named by prophets announced suffering / the servant bears and is wounded.

rightEvidence.title: The servant is rejected, wounded, silent, assigned a grave, and described as bearing sin

payload.tension: Peter makes a broad prophetic claim while Isaiah’s source preserves its own extended speaker, servant, and sequence.
payload.title: Prophets announced suffering / the servant bears and is wounded
